12	package com.sun.fortress.scala_src.typechecker.staticenv
13	
14	import com.sun.fortress.compiler.Types
15	import com.sun.fortress.nodes._
16	import com.sun.fortress.nodes_util.{NodeFactory => NF}
17	import com.sun.fortress.scala_src.nodes._
18	import com.sun.fortress.scala_src.useful.Lists._
19	import com.sun.fortress.scala_src.useful.Options._
20	import com.sun.fortress.useful.NI
21	
22	/**
23	 * Represents a list of variable name to static parameter bindings for some
24	 * context. All instances of this class should be created with `KindEnv.makeFresh`
25	 * or with the `extend` method.
26	 */
27	abstract sealed class KindEnv extends StaticEnv[StaticParam] {
28	
29	  /** My type. */
30	  type Env = KindEnv
31	
32	  /** My binding type. */
33	  type EnvBinding = KindBinding
34	
35	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given node. */
36	  def extend(node: Node): KindEnv =
37	    new NestedKindEnv(this, KindEnv.extractNodeBindings(node))
38	
39	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given nodes. */
40	  def extend[T <: Node](nodes: Iterable[T]): KindEnv =
41	    new NestedKindEnv(this, nodes.flatMap(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings))
42	
43	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given node. */
44	  def extend(node: Node, where: Option[WhereClause]): KindEnv = {
45	    val whereBindings = where.map(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings)
46	                             .getOrElse(Iterable.empty)
47	    val nodeBindings = KindEnv.extractNodeBindings(node)
48	    val declared = whereBindings ++ nodeBindings
49	    new NestedKindEnv(this, declared ++ KindEnv.constraintBounds(this, declared, where))
50	  }
51	
52	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given nodes. */
53	  def extend[T<:Node](nodes: Iterable[T], where: Option[WhereClause]): KindEnv = {
54	    val whereBindings = where.map(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings)
55	                             .getOrElse(Iterable.empty)
56	    val nodesBindings = nodes.flatMap(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings)
57	    val declared = whereBindings ++ nodesBindings
58	    new NestedKindEnv(this, declared ++ KindEnv.constraintBounds(this, declared, where))
59	  }
60	
61	  /**
62	   * Get the type of the given variable name, if it is bound. The resulting
63	   * type will only be defined if this name maps to a bool, int, or nat static
64	   * parameter.
65	   */
66	  def getType(x: Name): Option[Type] = lookup(x).flatMap(b =>
67	    b.sparam.getKind match {
68	      case _:KindBool => Some(Types.BOOLEAN)
69	      case _:KindInt => Some(Types.INT_LITERAL)
70	      case _:KindNat => Some(Types.INT_LITERAL)
71	      case _ => None
72	    })
73	
74	  def staticParam(x: Name): Option[StaticParam] = lookup(x).map(_.sparam)
75	}
76	
77	/** The single empty kind environment. */
78	protected object EmptyKindEnv extends KindEnv with EmptyStaticEnv[StaticParam] {
79	  // A type opened from a value is found in every environment, as a size
80	  // opened from a value needs no binding.
81	  override def lookup(x: Name): Option[KindBinding] = KindEnv.lookupOpened(x)
82	}
83	
84	/**
85	 * A kind environment with a parent and some explicit bindings.
86	 *
87	 * @param parent A kind environment that this one extends.
88	 * @param _bindings A collection of all the bindings in this environment.
89	 */
90	class NestedKindEnv (protected val parent: KindEnv,
91	                               _bindings: Iterable[KindBinding])
92	    extends KindEnv with NestedStaticEnv[StaticParam] {
93	
94	  /** Internal representation of `bindings` is a map. */
95	  val bindings: Map[Name, KindBinding] =
96	    Map(_bindings.map(b => (b.name, b)).toSeq:_*)
97	}
98	
99	/** Companion module for KindEnv; contains "static" members. */
100	object KindEnv extends StaticEnvCompanion[StaticParam] {
101	
102	  /** My type. */
103	  type Env = KindEnv
104	
105	  /** My binding type. */
106	  type EnvBinding = KindBinding
107	
108	  /** Creates a fresh kind environment. */
109	  def makeFresh: KindEnv = EmptyKindEnv.extend(Nil)
110	
111	  /**
112	   * The bindings that the where clause's trait constraints give: each type
113	   * variable X named by a constraint X extends B, bound in the declared
114	   * bindings or outside them, rebound with B added to its bounds.
115	   */
116	  def constraintBounds(outer: KindEnv, declared: Iterable[KindBinding],
117	                       where: Option[WhereClause]): Iterable[KindBinding] = where match {
118	    case Some(SWhereClause(_, _, constraints)) =>
119	      val scope = new NestedKindEnv(outer, declared)
120	      val byName = constraints.collect { case SWhereExtends(_, name, supers) => (name, supers) }
121	      val names = byName.map(_._1).foldLeft(List[Id]())((acc, n) =>
122	        if (acc.exists(_.getText == n.getText)) acc else acc :+ n)
123	      names.flatMap(n => scope.lookup(n) match {
124	        case Some(KindBinding(bn, sp)) if sp.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindType] =>
125	          val extra = byName.filter(_._1.getText == n.getText).flatMap(_._2)
126	          val supers = toListFromImmutable(sp.getExtendsClause) ++ extra
127	          List(KindBinding(bn, NF.makeStaticParam(sp, sp.getName.asInstanceOf[Id], toJavaList(supers))))
128	        case _ => Nil
129	      })
130	    case _ => Nil
131	  }
132	
133	  /** Extract out the bindings in node. */
134	  protected def extractNodeBindings(node: Node) : Iterable[KindBinding] =
135	    node match {
136	      // Trivially add this param.
137	      case p:StaticParam => Iterable(KindBinding(p.getName, p))
138	      
139	      // Extract bindings from generic declaration.
140	      case g:Generic =>
141	        toListFromImmutable(g.getHeader.getStaticParams)
142	          .map(p => KindBinding(p.getName, p))
143	      
144	      // Extract where clause bindings.
145	      case SWhereClause(info, bindings, _) => bindings.map {
146	        
147	        // If a type binding, create a new TypeParam.
148	        case b:WhereBinding if b.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindType] =>
149	          val sp = NF.makeTypeParam(info.getSpan, b.getName, b.getSupers, none[Type], false)
150	          KindBinding(b.getName, sp)
151	
152	        // A nat or int binding is a size, as a nat or int static parameter is.
153	        case b:WhereBinding if b.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindNat] || b.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindInt] =>
154	          val sp = NF.makeStaticParam(info.getSpan, null, b.getName,
155	                                      java.util.Collections.emptyList[BaseType],
156	                                      java.util.Collections.emptyList[BaseType],
157	                                      none[Type], false, b.getKind)
158	          KindBinding(b.getName, sp)
159	
160	        // Other kinds not supported yet.
161	        case _ => NI.nyi("non-type where clause bindings")
162	      }
163	
164	      case _ => Iterable.empty
165	    }
166	
167	  /* The types opened from values (TypeAnalyzer.openWhereSizes), each a fresh
168	   * name (Formula.openedSizeName) bound as its where-clause binding bounds it
169	   * at the trait's static arguments. A name is registered once and never
170	   * rebound, so an answer that reads its bound depends on the name alone. */
171	  private val opened = new java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap[String, KindBinding]()
172	
173	  def registerOpened(id: Id, sp: StaticParam): Unit = opened.put(id.getText, KindBinding(id, sp))
174	
175	  def lookupOpened(x: Name): Option[KindBinding] = x match {
176	    case i: Id if i.getApiName.isNone && i.getText.contains("#") => Option(opened.get(i.getText))
177	    case _ => None
178	  }
179	}
180	
181	/**
182	 * A binding for a kind environment contains name to static parameter pairs.
183	 *
184	 * @param name The variable name for the binding.
185	 * @param sparam The static parameter that this name is binding.
186	 */
187	case class KindBinding(name: Name,
188	                       sparam: StaticParam)

junit.sh
#!/bin/bash
# junit.sh <label> <dir-of-tests> <Name.test>... : the gather of climb batch N runs each .test through the
# harness in the main tree (fortress junit, the compiled test harness, as climb batch 6.5's gather ran its pair),
# in the order given, so that a link test runs before its XXX run test. Each named component's cache entries are
# removed before the list and after it. First line: the machine line (protocol.md, principle 2).
# ONE_JVM=1 (added 2026-09-29 for the repair on the merged tree, coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md, "A repair
# of tests and records only"): the whole list in one fortress junit run, one JVM, as the gate's track runs them
# together; Shell junit hands the list to FileTests.suiteFromListOfFiles (Shell.java:1086), which puts its
# compile and link tests before its run tests (FileTests.java:997-1004), so a link test still runs first.
# The environment is env.sh's, set here without sourcing it, since env.sh also removes parser directories in
# /tmp. The tree is the one this script is in. FORTRESS_THREADS=4 is the pin of build.xml's fastTrack macro,
# which runs the gate's compiled tracks. The JVMs keep their temporary files, parser directories among them,
# in the tree's tmp/.
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=4
mkdir -p "$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
FH=$FORTRESS_HOME; L=${1:?label}; D=$(cd "${2:?dir}" && pwd); shift 2
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress"
CP=$(../bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
echo "# junit.sh $L $(date -u +%FT%TZ); nproc $(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=$FORTRESS_THREADS; tree $(git -C $FH rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git -C $FH diff --quiet HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library || echo ' with the next rung applied, not yet committed'); tests from $D"
clean () { for t in "$@"; do n=$(sed -n 's/^tests=//p' "$D/$t" | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && find ../default_repository/caches -name "*$n*" -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; done; }
clean "$@"
if [ -n "${ONE_JVM:-}" ]; then
  files=(); for t in "$@"; do files+=("$D/$t"); done
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit, one JVM: $*"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "${files[@]}" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
else
for t in "$@"; do
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit $t"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "$D/$t" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
done
fi
clean "$@"

## 11. Decisions, findings, questions

**Decisions.** No decision of the curator covers 1 to 6.

1. **The split in order (variant B).** Rejected:
   - variant C, which tests `Node` first and skips 213 tests for leaves: 332 s against B's 344 s, one run
     each, within noise; its exactness needs a proof (every node class implements `Node`);
   - the JVM switch alone: 652 s, and a switch every JVM would need;
   - a class-keyed dispatch.
2. **30 cases per method.** The largest method is 4,474 bytes, against the limit of 8,000.
3. **The patch changes the generator and the file it writes, not the file alone.** A build would otherwise
   regenerate the old walker the next time `Fortress.ast` or a generator changes.
4. **An audit by branch index, not by memo hits.** The fix adds no memo.
5. **The test is in Java**, because of the scalac 2.13 limit (§8).
6. **The brief's "distance stage is `tools/count-run/`" read as `tools/distance/run.sh`.** `count-run.sh`
   runs each interpreter test under walk.

**Findings.**
- The interpreted walker (§2.2).
- The shares of the repair (+267 s) and of rung C (+109 s before the fix, +65 s after) (§3).
- After the fix, about 95 % of the component's time is in the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3).
- The checker's output depends on identity hashes (§9).
- The repair removes the distance stage's crash row and adds no site (§6).
- The other methods over the limit are negligible after the fix (§2.2).

**Defects.**
- **The interpreted walker.** My change repairs it (way 1), pinned by `WalkerJUTest`. No ledger row holds it;
  the row to write:
  - claim: the generated `Walker.walk` (`FortressAst.scala`, from `ScalaAstGenerator.java`) is 31,704 bytes
    of bytecode, past HotSpot's 8,000-byte huge-method limit, so the JVM never compiles it, and every phase
    that walks a tree runs it in the interpreter;
  - status: NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, closed by the fix's commit;
  - class: implementation gap (generator, speed);
  - spec: silent;
  - reproducer: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`;
  - found by: this probe.
- **The identity-hash dependence.** A note for row 488, with the H runs' commands and outputs (§9).

**Sentences of the specification made false:** none.

**For FACTS.**
1. **The fact.** The generated AST walker's `walk` was one method over HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit, so it ran
   interpreted. With it split in order, the count stage with row 680's repair takes 352 s instead of 911 s,
   and the distance stage 931 s instead of 2,375 s, with identical output.
   - What it means: row 680's line can land under the 690 s rule.
   - Test: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`.
   - Detail: §2.2 and §6.
2. **The fact.** The checker's output depends on the JVM's identity-hash sequence, because AST hashes include
   the `Class` identity hash. One extra identity hash at start reorders the api checks and the members of
   unions in messages.
   - What it means: the stages' outputs can move with an unrelated edit (row 488).
   - Command: the driver with `-Dprobe.hashes=1`.
   - Detail: §9.
3. **The fact.** Rung C's normal form costs 12 % of the count stage before the fix, 19 % after.
   - Detail: §3.

**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**
- Q1: land the walker split as its own rung ahead of row 680's line, or in the same rung?
- Q2: pursue the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3), about 95 % of what remains?
  - Ways: a memo of normalized meets shared across analyzers; fewer reductions in `Formula.and`'s fold.
- Q3: make AST hashing independent of identity hashes (row 488)? That would change iteration orders, and so
  message text, once.

**Commands worked out.**
- **JFR, read without the text dump.** A single-file Java program over `jdk.jfr.consumer.RecordingFile`
  aggregates `jdk.ExecutionSample` within an epoch window, by self, inclusive, callers or callees. A frame's
  `getType()` (Interpreted, JIT compiled, Inlined) shows which methods the JVM never compiled.
- **Methods over the limit:** a `java.lang.classfile` scan of `ProjectFortress/build` for `Code` attributes
  longer than 8,000 bytes.
- **The AST generators by hand, in scratch:**
  1. `javac -cp <scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar -d <dir>/build ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/*.java`.
  2. Copy `Fortress.ast` into `<dir>/astgen`.
  3. From there, `java -cp <dir>/build:<scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:astgen.jar edu.rice.cs.astgen.ASTGen Fortress.ast`. The `.ast` file's `customClassPath ../build` finds the generators.
- **A huge method's compile attempts:** `-XX:-DontCompileHugeMethods -XX:+PrintCompilation`.
- **Moving the identity-hash sequence:** a driver copy that calls `new Object().hashCode()` N times before
  the phases.

## 10. Decisions, findings, questions

**Decisions.**

1. I shared only answers whose computation read no context. This chooses exactness over reach. The alternatives:
   - TypeScript's rule, dualized: a true answer found under the history's cuts is true without them. It shares
     more, but it can change nested answers, and with them the per-analyzer normal forms.
   - Keys renamed apart, plus the variables' bounds, shared across analyzers.
   - Fuel or depth limits, which change answers.
   - Library-side changes: drop `IntLiteral` from `Number`'s clause, or keep `T extends Number`. These change the
     library, not the checker.
2. Only `True` and `False` are shared, not constraint formulas.
3. A hit in the analyzer's own memo counts as a context read. This is conservative.
4. The memo lives on `TraitTable`, behind its own switch, following rung M.
5. The refusal test carries the `XXX` prefix, by the team's convention.

No decision of the curator covers 1 to 5.

**Findings for the record.**

- The slowdown is recomputation, with the numbers of §2 and §3.
- The count stage on this tree takes about 300 s for the base, measured once at load 0.31. That is not "seconds",
  and the base's `checkApi FortressLibrary` takes 74 s under the fix.
- The overloading stage's error order is not fixed between runs (by reading, §7).
- Noticed by reading, not verified: `withClauseParams` decides by name whether a type variable in an excludes
  clause is in scope (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:820`). So an analyzer whose own parameter has the same name as the
  clause's could read the clause through its own bound. The fix counts that test as a context read.

**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**

- Q1: carry the fix as a rung ahead of fork 2's library half, or with it, or hold both until the distance stage's
  remaining gap (1,032 s against 819 s at the landed gate, not a pair) is also closed?
- Q2: pursue the further exact steps of §9?

**Commands worked out.**

- **Compile the fix into a shadow folder.** Two Scala files at once:
  `java -cp "$CP" scala.tools.nsc.Main -classpath "$CP" -d <dir> -encoding UTF-8 TraitTable.scala TypeAnalyzer.scala`.
  Then prefix `<dir>` to the classpath in copies of the stage scripts.
- **Run compiled `.test` files through the harness on shadow classes:**
  `FORTRESS_CACHES=$Q/caches java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfortress.caches=$Q/caches -cp "<dir>:$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit <absolute .test paths>`.
- **JFR with deep stacks:**
  `-XX:FlightRecorderOptions:stackdepth=2048 -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=...,settings=profile,dumponexit=true`.
  `jcmd <JVM pid> JFR.dump name=1 filename=...` takes a copy mid-run, and
  `jfr print --events jdk.ExecutionSample --stack-depth 2048` reads it.
  - The default 250 MB cap keeps only the last few minutes.
  - Aim `jstack` and `jcmd` at the `java` process, never at the stage's `timeout` wrapper. A dump aimed at the
    wrapper killed a run.

\subsection{Where-clause variables in extends clauses}
\seclabel{revival-where}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{where-clauses}; \secref{trait-decls}.
\item[Change] One sentence is added: a \KWD{where}-clause variable may not
appear as a static argument in an \KWD{extends} clause.
The three declarations that followed it are kept, marked
``Not allowed'', each with the way to write it
(\secref{revival-covariance}, \secref{revival-every},
\secref{revival-empty}).
A box after Victor Luchangco's two draft notes in \secref{trait-decls},
which say that a trait can explicitly extend itself through hidden type
variables and that ``we could just rule this a special case'', answers
them.
\item[Rationale] Such a variable makes the declared type a subtype of one
instantiation for each type the variable may stand for, and instantiation
exclusion forbids any two of them.
\item[Effect] None of the three declarations ran before the revision:
both implementations stop at name resolution, because a
\KWD{where}-clause variable is not in scope in an \KWD{extends} clause.
The revision makes that the rule.
The calculus of \appref{where-calculus} still admits such
declarations (\secref{revival-calculi}).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks

                             first 300 characters

                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order

        [--spec C] [--found-by C]

178	**A type parameter with two bounds, one a closed trait, in the checker**
179	
180	- Original: take `T extends { K, R[\T\] }`, with `K comprises { A, B, C }` and `C` not an `R`. The checker replaced `K` in such an intersection by the listed types that the other bound does not exclude, whatever that bound named. It also split a union on the right of a subtype question before it read the bound of a type variable, a static parameter in scope. So `T`'s bound became a union before the checker read it. The call `h(x)` in `g[\T extends { K, R[\T\] }\](x: Box[\T\])`, for an `h` with the same bounds, was refused ("is not applicable to an argument of type Box[\T\]"), or stopped the checker ("Applied a substitution to an And and got an Or"). A valid overloading beside it was refused by the return-type rule.
181	- Resolution: the checker expands a closed trait only against a bound that names no type variable or inference variable, the checker's placeholder for a static argument that it infers. An inference variable below a union takes the whole union as one upper bound. A type variable below a union is also tried through its bound. Such calls compile and run, and a call outside the bounds is refused as not applicable. Two cases still fail:
182	  - with a ground second bound, one that names no static parameter, the call is still refused: `h(x)` in `g[\T extends { K, Q }\](x: Box[\T\])`, where `Q` excludes a listed type (ledger row 712);
183	  - `f[\T extends { K, R[\T\] }\](x: T)` beside `f(x: Z)`, where `Z` excludes `A` and `B` and `C` extends `Z`, is refused as an invalid overloading, though the bound `R[\T\]` rules out `C` (ledger row 713).
184	- Reason: the specification makes such a call applicable at an instance within the bounds (`Specification/basic/inference.tex`). The type group's subtyping algorithm reads no `comprises` clause (`Papers/Types/fig-subtype.tick`). The POPL 2019 paper proves its matching complete only where no union holds a type parameter.
185	
186	**A `where` clause's constraint, in the checker**
187	
188	- Original: the traits chapter lets a `where` clause place constraints on static parameters (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex`). The checker read only a `where` clause's bindings, so it refused "No such method T.show." on a value of a constrained parameter.
189	- Resolution: a constraint bounds the variable that it names inside the declaration. A constraint on the declaration's own static parameter is part of its arrow, so the checker checks it at a call of a function or a functional method. Four cases are not built yet:
190	  - a method's constraint on its trait's or object's static parameter, at a dotted call (ledger row 748);
191	  - a constraint that bounds a type parameter by a `where`-clause variable: it refuses every call (ledger row 749);
192	  - a trait's or object's own constraint, where its type is used (ledger row 750);
193	  - a static argument written at a call, against its parameter's bound (ledger row 470).
194	- Reason: the chapter's rule. The library's fusion pairs need it ("The fusion of `SUM` with `MAX` and `MIN`", below).
195	
196	**Sizes on the compiled path**
197	
198	- Original: the Working Draft has the size parameters `nat` and `int`. The checker crashed on sized declarations, and a sized program did not compile or load. The team's code generator had reserved a slot for a size's run-time descriptor.
199	- Resolution: the checker checks sizes, and the slot holds the size's descriptor (`SKILL.md`, "The compiled run time").
200	- Reason: it completes the team's design, which carries a size as it carries a type argument.
201	
202	**Arithmetic in a size**
203	
204	- Original: the Working Draft allows a sum, a difference, a product or a power as a size, and fixes its value once the static parameters are known, but does not say when two such sizes are the same. The checker refused any arithmetic in a size, and counted a static parameter as different from every numeral. The compiled path spelled the expression into the class's name. Walk stopped on a power.
205	- Resolution: two sizes are the same when they are written alike once each operation on numerals is computed: `2 3` is `6`, and, for static parameters `s0` and `s1`, `s0 s1` is not `s1 s0`. A static parameter, or an expression with one in it, is not known to differ from a numeral, so in `typecase N[\b0\] of N[\0\] => ...`, for a static parameter `b0` and `NatReflect`'s object `N` (below), the arm `N[\0\]` is reachable. The checker checks a computed size against its parameter's kind, as it checks a numeral. It computes a power of 0, 1 or -1 at any exponent, and of another base up to the exponent 4096. It refuses a larger power as outside every kind. The compiled path computes a size when it names a class, so `Box[\2 + 1\]` and `Box[\3\]` are one class; the class loader does not check a size that it computes against its parameter's kind (ledger row 675). Walk computes a power exactly, as the compiled path does. Both compute no power at a negative exponent, which only a static parameter can give, and walk refuses it. The checker infers a size argument written as an operation on static parameters, as in `get(IBox[\i - 1\](0))` inside `pred[\int i\]()`.
206	- Reason: the library writes a product in the storage of its matrices, `mem: PrimitiveArray[\T, (s0 s1)\]` in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, and sums in result types. The grammar allows a power in a size. A `nat` or `int` parameter takes an integer, and a power at a negative exponent is no integer, except of 1 and -1. The team's questions and answers in the specification's appendix "Internal Document" (`Specification/appendices/internal-document.tex`) refuse two overloads at `T[\n+1\]` and `T[\0\]`.
207	
208	**A size known only at run time**
209	
210	- Original: `NatReflect`'s `reflect` answers a `NatParam`, a trait that the object `N[\nat n\]` extends (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fsi`). The team's clause of `NatParam`, `comprises { N[\n\] } where [\ nat n \]`, was a comment, and the api's comment says that a `NatParam` passed where `N[\n\]` is expected makes `n` a static parameter. The checker refused every such call in the library; walk ran them, binding the size at dispatch.
211	- Resolution: the clause is restored, and the specification allows a where-clause variable in a listed type. In the checker, a value of such a trait, passed where the listed type is expected, binds the call's `nat` parameter to the value's own size. That size is known to equal only itself: two values passed in one call have two sizes, and the size does not reach a type that names another size. Walk loads the clause and binds each size at dispatch, as before, so it runs such a call. The compiled run waits for the switch-over (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun.fss`).
212	- Reason: the team's comment, and the library's run-time factories, which pass `reflect`'s value to functions that take `N[\n\]`.
213	
214	**A type `where`-clause variable in a `comprises` clause**
215	
216	- Original: the team left `AnyList`'s clause `comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]` as a comment, "Not yet" (`Library/List.fsi`). The disambiguator, which both paths share, refused such a variable: "E is undefined." The checker refused four calls of `AnyList`'s and the comprehension's code, which read their arguments as a list of an unknown element type.
217	- Resolution: the clause is live. A trait's type `where`-clause variables are in scope in the trait, except in its `extends` and `excludes` clauses. At a call, the checker opens such a variable as it opens a size: the argument takes the listed type at a type of its own, bounded as the binding is, and known to equal only itself. It does not open such a trait where it reaches it as a parent. Walk binds the variable, when it loads the trait, as a type that stands for every type. `AnyList`'s `addLeft` and `addRight` are written with `||`. The departures:
218	  - the checker also opens the variable under a function type's result (ledger row 751);
219	  - it does not open an extender that the clause does not list (ledger row 752);
220	  - the checker and walk read the extenders at every type of a bounded variable (ledger rows 753 and 754);
221	  - walk refuses at load a member whose declared type names the variable, and the checker crashes at an outside call of one that names a type variable (ledger rows 755 and 756);
222	  - the code generator does not compile a trait with a `where` clause (ledger row 701).
223	- Reason: the team's comment, and the traits chapter, which lets a listed type hold a `where`-clause variable at every value of it (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations").
224	
225	**Comparing pairs and triples**

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT=/home/user/fortress-wherechecks/tmp/rung-checker-where-checks/ladder/root
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT=/home/user/fortress-wherechecks/tmp/rung-checker-where-checks/ladder
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"

# Source this in every shell that runs Fortress:  source explorations/experiment/env.sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=1
# bin/fortress defaults to -Xmx256m (gap ledger row 67); the checks at 4 threads override FORTRESS_THREADS on the command line
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m"
# every grammar-importing run leaves a 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory behind (RatsUtil.getTempDir); 723 of them filled the disk allowance on 2026-09-15.
# Remove only those that no run can still be using: nothing in it written for an hour, and no java process now
# running started before its last write (a run makes its directory after it starts, and reads it until it ends).
(
  oldest=$(ps -C java -o etimes= 2>/dev/null | sort -n | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
  now=$(date +%s)
  find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'fortress*rats' -mmin +60 -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null |
  while read -r t d ; do
    [ -n "$oldest" ] && [ "${t%.*}" -ge $(( now - oldest )) ] && continue
    [ -n "$(find "$d" -newermt '60 minutes ago' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && continue
    rm -rf "$d"
  done
)

## 1. What changed and why

All five rows are built, in the order the section gives.

- **Row 748.** `getCandidatesForMethod` (`Functionals.scala:973-1030`) drops a candidate whose where clause constrains its trait's or object's static parameter where the receiver's static argument breaks the constraint, so that candidate is not applicable and another overload is chosen. The methods come instantiated at the receiver; the argument for the trait's parameter is read off the instantiated method's self type, at the position of that parameter in its original's self type (`SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:56-81` builds both from the declaration's static parameters, in order). When every candidate is dropped the call is refused: "Method Holder[\String\].showIt is not applicable: its where clause requires String to extend Shows." The fold of a functional method's lifted arrow (`STypesUtil.scala:212-219`) is kept. Both callers of `getCandidatesForMethod`, the subscript and the method invocation (`Functionals.scala:1100` and `:1129`), get the check.
- **Row 749.** `makeArrowFromFunctional` (`STypesUtil.scala:195-220`) binds the where clause's own type, `nat` and `int` variables as static parameters of the arrow, after the declared ones, so the call infers them. That alone did not build the row: the arrow `[\U extends Object X[\n\], V extends Object Y[\n\], nat n\](U, V)->String` was still "not applicable to an argument of type (O, P)", because the solver fixes `U` and `V` from their lower bounds and kills nothing but type variables, then finds the size constraint `O <: X[\$n\]` left over and gives up (`Formula.scala:644-652`); its own comment says so: "TODO: We can solve more constraints if we iterate 1), 2) 3) until we hit a fixed point" (`Formula.scala:578`, the team's line, `:441` at `a874948ac`). `Formula.slv` now solves, once, what the type variables' solutions leave when it is sizes alone (`Formula.scala:649-656`); the retry runs only where the first attempt failed, so no call accepted before changes its solution. `GenericFnWithExcludes.fss:44`, `g(O, P)` with `P` a `Y[\2\]`, stays refused: no `n` meets both.
- **Row 750.** The trait-type case of `TypeWellFormedChecker.walk` (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:245-275`) checks the declaration's own trait constraints on its static parameters at the type's static arguments, with the bound's message. The constructor call `Wrap[\String\]("s")`, and `Wrap("s")` without a static argument, are refused through this case, at the call's type ("Ill-formed type: Wrap[\String\] The static argument String does not satisfy the corresponding bound Shows.", at `XXXWhereConstraintTypeUseChecker.fss:14:27-42`), not through the constructor's arrow, whose where clause (`STypesUtil.scala:178-181`) is not read at a call.
- **Row 753.** `checkDeclComprises` (`TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:318-333`) gives each type where-clause variable's inference variable its bounds, as a conjunct of the formula that `comprisesContains` solves (`:418-434`), passed through `isEligibleToExtend` and `everyKnownSubtypeListed`. `object NBox[\E extends Object\](item: E) extends AnyNumBox` is refused; `NBox[\E extends Number\]` is taken.
- **Row 771.** `whereSizes` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:856-882`) bounds a type where-clause variable by its binding and by each trait constraint of the clause on it, so `openWhereSizes`, unchanged, bounds the opened type by both, and the extender check of row 753 reads the same bounds (`XXXComprisesWhereConstraintExtenderChecker`).
- **Specification.** Appendix I's entry "The traits that extend a closed trait", its clauses on rows 771 and 753 (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1486-1500`), in the revision form, with the dates.

The rung's commits on `wip/rung-checker-where-checks`:

## FACTS

**The compiled checker checks a `where` clause's trait constraints where they apply.**
- A dotted call's candidate whose where clause constrains its trait's or object's static parameter is not applicable where the receiver's static argument breaks the constraint: 'Method Holder[\String\].showIt is not applicable: its where clause requires String to extend Shows.'
- A where clause's own type, `nat` and `int` variables are static parameters of the function's arrow, inferred at the call. So a constraint whose bound names one is met where some value of it meets every constraint. The solver fixes, once, a size that only the type variables' bounds name.
- A trait's or object's own constraint is checked where its type is used, with the bound's message; at a constructor call, the check is made on the call's type.
- A type `where`-clause variable of a `comprises` clause is bounded by its binding and by the clause's constraints on it, at its opening and in the extender check.
- Not read:
  - a constraint whose bound names the method's own static parameters or a `where`-clause variable, at a dotted call or at a type's use;
  - a static argument written at a top-level call (row 470).
- Walk still runs a dotted call that breaks a method's condition (NEW-K-2).
- The count stays 31 and the distance 35.

Tests: `XXXWhereBoundDottedCallChecker`, `WhereVariableBoundCallChecker`, `XXXWhereConstraintTypeUseChecker`, `XXXWhereConstraintExtendsChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereBoundExtenderChecker`, `OpenTypeWhereConstraintChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereConstraintExtenderChecker`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-where-checks/REPORT.md`, sections 1 and 6.

Entries this makes false, for the gather to rewrite:
- F-250's holes on rows 748, 750 and 749; row 470's stays;
- F-244's "is not checked at a dotted call (row 748; F-250)" and "The built forms' other departures are rows 749 to 753 and 771";

- **Row 748,** test `XXXWhereBoundDottedCallChecker`. Close note: a constraint whose bound names the method's own static parameters or a `where`-clause variable is not read at the dotted call; walk's sibling is NEW-K-2.
- **Row 749,** test `WhereVariableBoundCallChecker` (promoted from `XXXWhereVariableBoundCall`). Close note: the arrow binds the clause's variables only when the clause has a trait constraint; the solver's retry is in `Formula.slv`; `GenericFnWithExcludes.fss:44` stays refused, since no `n` meets both constraints, and walk runs it.
- **Row 750,** test `XXXWhereConstraintTypeUseChecker` (with `XXXWhereConstraintExtendsChecker`). Close note: the constructor call is refused through the call's type in the trait-type case, not through the constructor's arrow; a constraint whose bound names a `where`-clause variable is not read.

- **Row 771,** test `OpenTypeWhereConstraintChecker` (promoted from `XXXOpenTypeWhereConstraintChecker`). Close note: the extender check reads the constraint's bound too (`XXXComprisesWhereConstraintExtenderChecker`).

Climb batch 18 rung K: the compiled checker checks `where` conditions where they apply, at a dotted call, through a `where`-clause variable at a call, at a type's use and in a `comprises` clause's opening and extender check (rows 748, 749, 750, 753 and 771); the solver solves once the sizes its type variables' bounds leave; count 31 and distance 35 unchanged; NEW-K-1 (the outer of two nested calls not reported) and NEW-K-2 (walk runs a dotted call that breaks a method's condition) recorded.

## Revival change

### The change

1. **A `where` clause's constraint, in the checker.**
   - What the team's sources do:
     - The team's compiled checker read a `where` clause's type bindings and none of its constraints: `case SWhereClause(info, bindings, _)`, with its other kinds `NI.nyi("non-type where clause bindings")` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/staticenv/KindEnv.scala:118-126` at `a874948ac`).
     - Walk checks an object's own constraint at a use of its type ('String must subtype Shows'). But it runs a dotted call that breaks a method's condition on its object's parameter: `Holder[\String\]("s").showIt()` prints `h` (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXWhereBoundDottedCallWalk.fss`, ledger NEW-K-2).
     - The team's test `ProjectFortress/tests/GenericFnWithExcludes.fss:44` calls `g(O, P)` with `O` an `X[\1\]` and `P` a `Y[\2\]`, for `g[\U, V\](u: U, v: V) where [\nat n\]{U extends {X[\n\]}, V extends {Y[\n\]}}`, and expects it to run (`:45`). Walk runs it.
   - What the tree's checker now does:
     - It refuses a dotted call whose every candidate breaks its `where` clause's constraint on its trait's or object's static parameter, and it passes over such a candidate for another: 'Method Holder[\String\].showIt is not applicable: its where clause requires String to extend Shows.' (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXWhereBoundDottedCallChecker.test`).
     - It infers a `where`-clause variable that a constraint's bound names. So `g(O, P)` with `P` a `Y[\1\]` is accepted (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/WhereVariableBoundCallChecker.test`), and the team's `g(O, P)` with `P` a `Y[\2\]` stays refused, since no `n` meets both.
     - It refuses a type, and a constructor call, whose static argument breaks the declaration's own constraint: 'Ill-formed type: Wrap[\String\] The static argument String does not satisfy the corresponding bound Shows.' (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXWhereConstraintTypeUseChecker.test`, `XXXWhereConstraintExtendsChecker.test`).
   - Not built:
     - a constraint whose bound names the method's own static parameters or a `where`-clause variable, at a dotted call or a type's use;
     - a static argument written at a top-level call (ledger row 470).
   - Reason:
     - "Static parameters may have constraints placed on them in a where clause" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex`, "Where Clauses").
     - The where calculus checks a method's bounds at a dotted call and asks for witnesses of the `where`-clause variables (`Specification/appendices/calculi/where/static.tex:241-257` and `:287-324`). It reads a type as well-formed only at such witnesses (`:399-410`).
2. **A type `where`-clause variable in a `comprises` clause.**
   - What the checker did before: in the extender check it read a listed type at every type of the variable, whatever its bound, and it bounded an opened type by the binding alone.
   - What it does now: in both places, it reads the listed type at the types below the variable's binding's bound and the clause's constraints on it.
     - `object NBox[\E extends Object\](item: E) extends AnyNumBox`, for `trait AnyNumBox comprises { NBox[\E\] } where [\E extends Number\]`, is refused (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXComprisesWhereBoundExtenderChecker.test`).
     - An extender outside a constraint is refused too (`XXXComprisesWhereConstraintExtenderChecker.test`).
     - `fooOf(mk())`, with `fooOf[\E extends Foo\](b: Box[\E\])` and `trait AnyBox comprises { Box[\E\] } where [\E\] { E extends Foo }`, is accepted (`OpenTypeWhereConstraintChecker.test`).
   - Walk still reads every type at load (ledger row 754).
   - Reason: a listed type holds at every value of the variable, and an extender is a subtype of a listed type (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations").

### Provenance

- P-151, "Only the `where` forms the team wrote down are built": a method's `where` condition bounds its static parameters. The checks left beside the forms that the climb batch before built are built here.
- The coordinator's call on the peers' way of checking a method's constraint at a call, in PLAN's phase 3 line on where clauses, listed for the curator.
- Climb batch 18, rung K.
